Julie — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. I looped in Marissa and Karthik for pricing/legal so we can get a consolidated response. A few quick points from our side after a first pass:

- Bridging slab approach: we like the intent (smoother economics) but need to confirm how it maps to our batching/caching assumptions. Request to OrbitSoft legal: can you call out the exact audit log retention window you're requesting in the redline? Our standard is 90 days plus on-request export for 1 year.

I'll put together a counter that preserves the bridging slab intent but ties floors/credits to MAS and a quarterly true-up. Marissa — can you advise on the MAS threshold we'd be willing to accept for a year-one floor? Karthik — any legal pitfalls on the proposed audit language?

Julie / team —

Thanks for sending the redlines. We reviewed with Finance & Legal; below is our proposed counter that should be acceptable to both sides:

1) Bridging slab mechanics — ACCEPT IN PRINCIPLE
- We'll implement a three-slab bridging structure. Instead of sudden jumps at breakpoints, tokens in the overlapping band will be billed at a weighted average of adjacent slabs (calculation in Exhibit B). This keeps your smoothing intent while keeping our runtime cost coverage predictable.

2) Floor / downside protection — CONDITIONAL
- Redwood can agree to a 5% price floor for year one but requires a minimum annual spend (MAS) of $450,000. If OrbitSoft cannot commit to MAS, floor reduces to 2% for the first 12 months. True-up applies at year-end.

3) Burst credits / reconciliation — COUNTERPROPOSAL
- Redwood will provide a Q4 burst pool equal to 15% of committed monthly capacity for one quarter. Any usage above committed + burst will be invoiced at list rates and then subject to a quarterly true-up with a maximum cap of 10% net credit (if overall usage exceeds projections materially, we apply regular overage billing).

4) Audit log retention — LIMITED AGREEMENT
- We can export audit logs on request for up to 12 months; default retention is 90 days. For regulated audits we can provide a one-time export package. We cannot provide continuous extended retention in-host without a platform change request.

Next steps: if OrbitSoft agrees in principle, we will prepare a clean counter order form and updated Pricing Exhibit (with the bridging slab math) and circulate for signatures. Also propose a 30-minute call Monday to review the MAS number and finalize the DocuSign link.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

- Bridging slab: the weighted-average approach looks fine; procurement asked for a worked example using Q3 projected usage — I'll upload that to the linked Drive by EOD Sunday.

- Burst credits: 15% Q4 pool is acceptable provided the reconciliation is quarterly and capped at the percentage you noted. We will need the reconciliation formula in Exhibit C.

If you can update the Order Form to show the 3% floor at $400k and an alternative pathway to 5% at $425k with a 6-month review, we should be able to get internal approvals quickly. Once that's in the clean counter we'll route to DocuSign.
